title: Relative external sections and induced rational coactions
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $X,Y$ be schemes over $\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. For a module sheaf $F$ on $X$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], let $\Gamma_R(X,F)$ be $\Gamma(X,F)$ with scalars restricted along $R\simeq\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}R,\mathcal O)\to\Gamma(X,\mathcal O)$. Pullback of a section along $a$ is the section $1\otimes s$ in the tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback], restricted from $a^{-1}(X)$ to the top open. For $P=X\times_RY$ [def-pc-fibre-product] with projections $p_X,p_Y$, put $E(F,G)=p_X^*F\otimes p_Y^*G$ using the existing sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and define $e(s,t)=p_X^*s\otimes p_Y^*t\in\Gamma(P,E(F,G))$. The comparison of pullbacks across a commutative square is the composite of the section-normalized composition identifications and the equality of composite scheme maps. For $a:X'\to X,b:Y'\to Y$ over $R$, define $(a\times b)^*E(F,G)\simeq E(a^*F,b^*G)$ by the section-normalized tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-tensor] and the two projection squares. Let $H$ be an affine group scheme over $R$ with canonical coordinate Hopf algebra $C=R[H]$ [def-sfb-affine-coordinate-hopf-algebra]. If $H$ acts on $X,Y$, use the action-groupoid presentation [def-sfb-equivariant-coherent-gzero] and the existing groupoid module [def-sfb-scheme-groupoid-module] for a quasi-coherent linearized module: its descent isomorphism is $\beta_F:a_X^*F\simeq\operatorname{pr}_X^*F$, the inverse of the forward linearization. The diagonal action on $P$ is the unique map with components $a_X\circ(1_H\times p_X)$ and $a_Y\circ(1_H\times p_Y)$. Its external descent is the tensor of $\beta_F,\beta_G$ pulled back along $1_H\times p_X,1_H\times p_Y$, with the above composition and tensor comparisons. A rational coaction means the existing counital coassociative $R$-linear right coaction [def-sfb-affine-group-distribution-calculus], using module tensor products [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. It is induced by a descent isomorphism $\beta$ if for every finite presentation $\rho(s)=\sum_i s_i\otimes c_i$ one has $\beta(a^*s)=\sum_i\operatorname{pr}_H^*(S(c_i))\operatorname{pr}_X^*(s_i)$, where $S$ is the antipode of $C$; thus $\rho$ is the right coaction of the left module $(h\cdot s)(x)=s(h^{-1}x)=\sum_ic_i(h)s_i(x)$, which is what makes it compatible with $(\rho\otimes1)\rho=(1\otimes\Delta)\rho$ for a left action of a noncommutative $H$. These are definitions of actual sections, comparisons, and the induced-coaction predicate; no section base-change isomorphism is assumed.
